teach_overlay.scale: a twenty-letter RNA guide offers more than one trillion possible four-letter combinations — over three hundred times more addresses than there are letters in the entire three-billion-letter human genome, letting Cas9 find one exact genetic street address inside a cell

plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period parchment, an inked gene-editing reprogramming comparison chart contrasts earlier protein-guided nucleases (ZFNs and TALENs, requiring months of custom 3D protein engineering per DNA target) against RNA-guided CRISPR-Cas9 (1 universal Cas9 endonuclease + interchangeable 20-nucleotide guide RNA synthesized in hours).

teach_overlay.label: CUSTOM PROTEIN NUCLEASES (MONTHS PER TARGET) VS UNIVERSAL CAS9 + 20-NT GUIDE RNA (HOURS PER TARGET)
teach_overlay.detail: Inked gene-editing reprogramming comparison chart contrasting protein-guided nucleases (new 3D protein required for every DNA sequence) against RNA-guided CRISPR-Cas9 (1 universal Cas9 endonuclease + interchangeable 20-nt guide RNA)
teach_overlay.scale: before CRISPR, targeting a new gene was like forging a brand-new steel key from scratch for every door in a city — whereas with CRISPR-Cas9, the steel scissors stay the same and you simply type a new twenty-letter postcode onto a strip of RNA
